newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Dutch PTT bid for Australia's TNT seen successful.
newsitem.headline: Dutch PTT bid for Australia's TNT seen successful.

text.p: Dutch telecommunications and postal group Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV (KPN) Wednesday launched a $1.6 billion takeover bid for worldwide transport group TNT Ltd, seeking to create Europe's largest fast-delivery shipping business.
If combined, KPN-TNT would be in the world's top four time-sensitive freight and logistics groups and have annual revenues of over A$6.0 billion (US$4.4 billion).
The enlarged KPN would offer services in 200 countries with its own operations in 47 countries and carry more than two million items of freight a week.
Australian-based TNT Ltd said in a joint statement with KPN it would recommend shareholders accept KPN's A$2.45 per share cash offer -- 50 percent above TNT's previous closing share price.
Analysts and brokers said the size of the premium and TNT's recommendation meant the bid was likely to deter any potential rivals, such as Federal Express Corp., and ensure the takeover goes through.
"What they've done is said, 'We don't want to get into a bidding war -- here's A$2.45 -- end of story'," said ABN AMRO Hoare Govett transport analyst Damien Horth.
KPN is 45 percent owned by the Dutch government.

KPN and TNT said the takeover agreement followed long discussions between KPN and TNT about combining TNT's GD Express Worldwide time sensitive freight and logistics business with KPN's postal subsidiary, PTT Post.
"It will create a new global force in the time-sensitive distribution and logistics industry, ranking in the top four worldwide," KPN and TNT said.
Shareholders and brokers immediately welcomed the bid, pushing TNT's share price up 50 percent to A$2.44 in early trade.
The shares eased back to A$2.42 at the close, with KPN confirming it had bought 9.9 percent of TNT's shares in the market.
KPN chairman and chief executive Wim Dik said the TNT acquisition would help KPN grow quickly outside its home market.
KPN said it would fund the takeover from working capital and and a 2.25 billion guilders (A$1.7 billion) revolving credit facility arranged and underwritten by Goldman Sachs.

Dik said the acquisition would be slightly earnings positive in the calendar 1997 year. He said KPN would consider whether to sell TNT assets not related to time-sensitive freight and logisitics within the next year.
Ratings agency Standard and Poors Corp later affirmed KPN's AA plus long-term credit rating and put TNT's B plus rating on credit watch positive.
